appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Gallardon presents her nephew — "Adalbert, tu sais, le fameux oncle Palamède dont tu entends toujours parler" — and Charlus answers "« Bonsoir, madame de Gallardon »... et il ajouta sans même regarder le jeune homme : « Bonsoir, Monsieur », d'un air bourru et d'une voix si violemment impolie, que tout le monde en fut stupéfait."
appraisal_events.explanation: A presentation is staged and refused in front of the room: the young man is greeted without a glance and in a tone that leaves the bystanders stupefied, and the aunt who staged it is refused with him.

appraisal_events.evidence: "ce Don Quichotte s'était battu contre tant de moulins à vent" that the Guermantes now heed his exclusives "qu'une fois sur deux"; foreseeing that one day it will be he who is done without, "il avait commencé à faire la part du feu, à baisser, comme on dit, ses prix"; his rages are too frequent to build "un fond de haine où construire" and he howls alone at home over a letter. When the narrator asks to be presented to the Prince he snaps "Hé bien, si vous les connaissez, en quoi avez-vous besoin de moi pour vous présenter" and turns his back on him.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator sets out, at length and in his own voice, the erosion of Charlus's power to exclude, and the snapped refusal that leaves the narrator without a sponsor is offered as one more fragmentary explosion rather than a real veto.

appraisal_events.evidence: "je compris tout de suite que l'homme foncièrement dédaigneux était le duc qui vous parlait dès la première visite de « pair à compagnon », et que des deux cousins celui qui était vraiment simple c'était le Prince"; his stiffness holds "plus de simplicité réelle et, quand on les connaît davantage, plus de bonté... dans leur hauteur traditionnelle que de plus modernes dans l'affectation de la camaraderie badine", and his distant question about the narrator's career is asked "par bonne grâce".
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator revises the received view — the duke's famous affability is the true contempt — and awards the prince's cold reserve the real simplicity and consideration.

appraisal_events.evidence: "le mot « bonsoir » fut susurré à mon oreille par M. de Bréauté... comme la voix d'un sauveur possible"; "ayant entendu ma demande, il l'accueillit avec satisfaction, me conduisit vers le Prince et me présenta à lui d'un air friand, cérémonieux et vulgaire, comme s'il lui avait passé, en les recommandant, une assiette de petits fours", and the Prince receives him and asks about his career.
appraisal_events.explanation: After the refusals the presentation finally takes place and the narrator is received by the host himself; the same sentences render Bréauté as a snuffling, greedy connoisseur of elegance passing him round like a plate of petits fours.

status_effects.explanation: Brought up to be admitted to the famous uncle's acquaintance, he is left outside it — greeted without a look and dismissed before the whole room.
Her right as a cousin to present her own nephew is publicly refused, and the bystanders' stupefaction registers the rebuff as an event.
The narration reduces his terribleness to Don Quixote's windmills and to rages so frequent and so short-lived that they cancel one another.
His standing in the family is registered as falling: his bans are obeyed only every other time and he has begun lowering his prices for fear of being the one dispensed with.
At the first attempt the door stays shut: the only sponsor he has turns his back and returns to his cards, leaving him unpresented in the host's house.
A separate moment and a different sponsor carry him across the line he was held at: he is led to the Prince, presented, greeted and questioned as a guest properly received.
The passage's considered verdict reverses the salon's: his hauteur is credited with real simplicity, goodness and consideration.
He loses by the same comparison: his cordial familiarity is named as the fundamentally disdainful manner of the two cousins.
The service he renders is narrated as caricature — the sniffing that will let no elegance escape, the dilated nostrils, the manner at once dainty, ceremonious and vulgar.

ambiguities: The passage also reports that the Prince swept Swann off to the far end of the garden "même, dirent certaines personnes, « afin de le mettre à la porte »" — a possible public expulsion given only as hearsay in a single clause; it is left unrecorded here rather than weighed against the four dominant movements.
